title: Score Equating Across AI Safety Benchmarks: Enabling Valid Cross-Benchmark Model Comparisons

original_idea.body:
# Score Equating Across AI Safety Benchmarks: Enabling Valid Cross-Benchmark Model Comparisons

**Problem:** P9: Can't compare models across different safety benchmarks

**Direction:** Apply IRT-based score equating to link scores from two different AI safety benchmarks (e.g., HarmBench and MLCommons AI Safety Benchmark) using a common set of anchor models evaluated on both, placing all models on a common safety ability scale.

**Why it matters:** Currently, a model's score on HarmBench cannot be directly compared to its score on MLCommons ASB. Score equating—the standard psychometric solution for this problem—would for the first time allow cross-benchmark model comparisons and enable tracking of safety progress across benchmark generations.

**Relevant context:** IRT equating is described as 'the process of equating test forms to ensure scores are comparable no matter what set of items an examinee sees' (Assessment Systems). A 2025 paper on psychometric benchmarks for generalist medical AI (PMC 2025) applies similar linking approaches to medical AI benchmarks. Anchor models evaluated on multiple benchmarks are available via leaderboards.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: score equating enables cross-benchmark safety comparisons and longitudinal tracking. Important infrastructure but the link to directly reducing catastrophic risk has a gap.

low_compute.reasoning: IRT equating in R (mirt) on existing data. CPU-only.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: IRT equating requires understanding anchor models and equating methods. Intermediate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: equate two safety benchmarks using common anchor models. Clear deliverable but requires identifying overlapping model evaluations.

quick_reasoning: Directly addresses the inability to compare models across different safety benchmarks with a concrete IRT equating approach.
